Hybrid

/HY-brid/ — rhymes with timid · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A hybrid is something formed by combining two different things, so that it carries features of both.

The mule is a hybrid of a horse and a donkey.

Worked Example

After years of research, the botanist finally created a hybrid rose that combined the fragrance of the heritage variety with the disease-resistance of the wild species.

This rose perfectly shows what hybrid means: it's not just a heritage rose or just a wild rose, but one plant carrying features of both. The word hybrid is more precise than saying 'rose' or 'plant' because it captures that this specific flower results from two different types merged into one unified entity.

How Hybrid Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

mixture

mixture: a combination of different things

blend

blend: a smooth mix of two or more things

combination

combination: two or more things joined together

Antonyms

pure

pure: made of only one thing, not mixed

purebred

purebred: descended from a single, unmixed breed or line

How Strong Is It? — separate → mixture → fusion → hybrid

separate vs. hybrid

separate vs. hybrid: Separate is the starting point, two things kept fully apart — the opposite of a hybrid, which combines them into one that carries features of both.

mixture vs. hybrid

mixture vs. hybrid: A mixture just puts things loosely together, but a hybrid is a truer blend, a single new thing that inherits qualities from both of its parents.

fusion vs. hybrid

fusion vs. hybrid: Fusion is even more complete than a hybrid: in a hybrid the two sources stay recognizable, while in a fusion they merge so fully they can no longer be told apart.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — hybrid

Root — hybrid: crossbred offspring; mongrel (from Latin 'hybrida') (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Hybrid comes from the Latin 'hybrida,' meaning a crossbred animal such as the offspring of a tame sow and a wild boar — capturing today's sense of something made by combining two different kinds into one.

Use the root in a new word: hybridize

Use the root in a new word: hybridize: When gardeners hybridize two kinds of rose, they cross them to create a hybrid — the verb built directly from the same word.

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral / technical

Hybrid is the precise term when you need to emphasize that something combines two distinct types into one unified entity. For general mixing or blending, plainer words like 'mixture' or 'blend' work fine, but only 'hybrid' captures the specific idea of two different things merged together.
